material.text: Diagnostic analysis on 30 COCO images with 5 prompt templates revealed that shallow-layer attention in InternVL2.5-8B is highly prompt-stable (cosine similarity [math] across prompts) but exhibits weak position correlation (Spearman [math] , well below the 0.3 threshold for meaningful positional bias).
Position correlation is uniformly weak ( [math] 0.17) at all layers, well below the 0.3 threshold for meaningful positional bias.
This explains why ratio-based debiasing fails.
Table xxrefxx presents diagnostic metrics from our Phase-0 analysis on 30 COCO images with 5 prompt templates (150 forward passes).
The key finding is that position correlation (Spearman [math] between attention and token position) is uniformly weak across all layers, ranging from 0.143 to 0.179.
All values are well below the 0.3 threshold typically considered indicative of meaningful positional bias.
This explains why ratio-based debiasing fails: there is no position-specific bias to correct in InternVL2.5-8B's attention patterns.
